What I Carry: What I Carry Field Notes on Symbol Work I carry six prepared configurations at any time. Three containment variants... I adjust which three depending on the expected entity type. One banishment. One communication, for the spirit encounters where talking is the right approach. One that I developed myself in year four, a slow-acting disruption configuration, which I keep having to re-explain to Grid contacts who find it on me because it does not look like anything in their standard reference. I prepare everything in advance. I have never successfully prepared a configuration in the field under active threat. I have tried twice. Both times I used what I had already made, and both times the situation resolved or did not resolve on the basis of what was already in my kit, not what I attempted to draw while something was actively trying to get into my perimeter. Prepare in advance. This is the only advice on symbol work that matters before you learn the rest. The configuration I use most often is the threshold ward. I have a standard set pre-drawn and folded in the left front pocket of every bag I own. I replace them weekly whether or not I have used them because I do not want to reach for one and find it degraded. The most powerful thing I carry is the exorcism circle, in five parts, sealed separately. I have used it once in six years. I prepared for it for three months before the operation. The preparation made the difference. The configurations themselves... what they are, how to draw them, what they require, what they cost... are in the technical documentation.
